_help: Checked coins. A coin is ranked only when its circulating supply is read by us from the chain (supply.method). 'exclude' lists wallets that are not circulating, with a reason; they show on the coin page. 'venues' limits which exchange markets count (e.g. {} = only its own pools). 'pools' adds DEX pools we read directly. Approved listings from the 'List your coin' form are added here by tools/listings.mjs.

supply.note: New AERO contract only: the legacy Aerodrome token 0x940181a9...8631 was retired on 22 Oct 2026 and its holders migrate 1:1, so its supply is not added on top. Aero's upgrade page publishes circulating AERO as total less sAERO, and of that maximum a further ~286M sits unclaimed in the two migration vaults and never reaches circulation unless upgraded. Excluding sAERO plus both vaults leaves circulating + unclaimed vault balance = total less sAERO = the published ~1.07B maximum. No max is published here because the reported 2,127,000,000 was below the live total supply.

Circulating supply is not published. Quant's own 14 Sep 2018 burn post gives the post-burn total 14,612,493.080826178 QNT, of which 9,964,259.03181537 was public and 4,648,234.049010808 was held by the company. The public figure is a 2018 snapshot, not today's circulating supply, and Quant has disclosed nothing about how much of the company allocation it still holds: Blockworks' disclosure file records no current figure, the only Etherscan-labelled company figure is ~68,000 QNT and is unreconciled with the 2018 number, and community estimates of ~2M in treasury carry no source. Subtracting the 2018 company balance would assume none of it was ever sold; skipping it would assume all of it was. Both overstate or understate without proof, so circulating stays unpublished rather than guessed, per the rule that circulating is never overstated. Total supply, which is what this rule publishes, is fixed: the contract has no mint function and Quant's burn set it once.

Ethereum ERC-20 BLUR only (single chain, no multichain parts). Token identity and the 3,000,000,000 max are the two Etherscan pages that resolve: https://etherscan.io/token/0x5283D291DBCF85356A21bA090E6db59121208b44 is titled Blur (BLUR) and shows Max Total Supply 3,000,000,000 BLUR, and the verified source https://etherscan.io/address/0x5283D291DBCF85356A21bA090E6db59121208b44#code is contract BlurToken (ERC20 name Blur, symbol BLUR) with constant INITIAL_SUPPLY = 3_000_000_000, minted once in the constructor and with no later mint. That constant is max. Circulating is withheld: Blur publishes no addresses for the contracts holding the core-contributor, launch-partner, advisor and community-treasury allocations, so those balances cannot be subtracted from primary sources. The only provable non-circulating wallet is the burn address, which the rule reads and records as an exclusion. Publishing total-minus-burn as circulating would overstate it, so we publish the chain-read total and this sourced max, and withhold circulating (the SEI treatment from bounty #3).
